title: Fog
description: Looking straight up between the Canary Wharf towers into a summer cumulus sky, with air that knows how far away everything is. Drag up or scroll to shorten the visibility, down to clear it; the haze gathers a little thicker wherever the pointer rests. The far towers go first, turning the blue of the sky they stand in, the cumulus fade behind the veil while their edges stay crisp, and the glass corner overhead stays sharp in front of it all.
intent: Aerial perspective, after Makoto Shinkai's skyward city shots and the worm's-eye summer photographs herb loves: converging towers, a cobalt zenith, cumulus. Beer-Lambert transmittance per pixel and per channel (Rayleigh-leaning, blue extinguished first) through a haze layer that thins with height, along a metric distance converted from a Depth Anything V2 map. Drag sets the meteorological visibility (Koschmieder, beta = 3.912 / V) from 50 km to 200 m. The in-scattered light comes from the sky itself: a normalised wide blur of the sky pixels only, so distance turns things blue, never grey. The sky is seen through a thinner column of the haze than the street, and the haze in front of it only veils it: forward-scatter softening touches the towers, never the clouds. The plate is two Poly Haven HDRIs (CC0, from their 16k captures) rendered at 3840 through the same stereographic rays: canary_wharf for the towers, docklands_01 for the sky, its cumulus split-graded warm-neutral on the sunlit tops and skylight blue in the folds. A film finish runs last: a diffusion bloom, a filmic shoulder whose top end lands the cloud tops near #FFF1E2, glass graded away from the sky's blue, a thin red halation under the highlight edges, and 24 fps grain at scan scale held for two frames.
